title: Broken or not? cases
subject: Islamic Studies
source: Written for islamic-studies/y7 lesson 25 (Pupil PDF worksheet: broken or not? cases)
intro: Lesson 25: What invalidates salah (mubtilat). Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Small movements are fine
points: The Prophet ﷺ carried his granddaughter Umamah in salah
Small, needed movements do not break it

questions.a: Not broken: a small, needed movement.

questions.q: Turning the whole body to see who came in.
questions.a: Broken: turning away from the qiblah. (Just glancing is disliked, not breaking.)
Broken: pray again. (Smiling does not break it.)

questions.q: Eating a sweet that was in the mouth.
Picking up a small child who needs it, then putting them down.
questions.a: Not broken: the Prophet ﷺ carried his granddaughter Umamah in salah.

questions.q: Explain why speaking breaks salah but a small movement to silence a phone does not.
questions.a: Speaking is not part of salah and is forbidden in it; a small needed movement is allowed, as the Prophet ﷺ carried Umamah.

questions.q: Eight 'broken or not?' cases on the pupil PDF, with the rule and evidence (e.g. sneezing and saying alhamdulillah quietly; scratching once; a cat walks in front; turning to see who came in).
questions.a: Rulings with rules: sneeze and quiet alhamdulillah: not broken; scratch once: not broken; cat: not broken; turning the body away: broken, glancing: disliked

questions.q: Extend: list three things that harm khushu' without breaking salah.
Stretch: how can we build khushu' online at home?
questions.a: Pray in a quiet place, phone away, know the meanings of what we recite.

questions.q: Yusuf laughs out loud at a noise during salah. His salah is ...
questions.a: A) Broken: he must pray again. Laughing aloud breaks salah; smiling does not.

questions.q: Think again: phone buzzes: ignore, silence or answer?
questions.a: Ignore or silence with a small movement; answering breaks salah.
